# Adjudication Task — Chapter 51

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃51화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|쉬쉬쉭!
  6|
  7|검, 도끼, 철퇴.
  8|
  9|수십 개의 무기가 소나기처럼 쏟아졌다. 그러나 내게는 똑똑히 보인다. 공격 하나하나가 어디로, 어떻게 향하는지.
 10|
 11|그 틈을 파고들었다.
 12|
 13|서걱-
 14|
 15|C급 몬스터, 리자드맨 전사의 목을 쳐 날리는 게 시작이었다. 창날이 반원을 그림과 동시에 사방에서 핏물이 솟구쳤다.
 16|
 17|띠링. 띠링. 띠링.
 18|
 19|
 20|
 21|- [Lv.40 리자드맨 전사]를 처치했습니다!
 22|
 23|- [Lv.41 늪지대 리자드맨]을 처치했습니다!
 24|
 25|- [Lv.40 늪지대 리자드맨]을…….
 26|
 27|
 28|
 29|- 키이이…….
 30|
 31|살아남은 놈들이 주춤거리며 물러선다. 동족의 원수를 만나 살기를 뿜어내던 녀석들이, 지금은 두려움에 떨고 있다.
 32|
 33|하지만 그것도 잠시.
 34|
 35|- 크워어어!
 36|
 37|
 38|
 39|- 보스 몬스터, [Lv.52 리자드맨 대족장]이 출현했습니다!
 40|
 41|- 스킬, [전장의 함성]을 사용합니다!
 42|
 43|
 44|
 45|최소 두 배는 큰 덩치. 거대한 철퇴를 든 리자드맨 족장의 외침에 공기가 터져 나간다. 우두머리의 등장에 뒷걸음질 치던 리자드맨들이 정신을 차리고 대열을 갖췄다.
 46|
 47|‘어쩐 일로 쉽게 끝나나 했다.’
 48|
 49|등 뒤로 최 팀장의 느긋한 목소리가 들렸다.
 50|
 51|“가능하겠어요?”
 52|
 53|“그게 며칠 동안 손 하나 까딱 안 한 사람이 할 소립니까?”
 54|
 55|“이야기가 다르죠. C급 게이트니까.”
 56|
 57|“그럼 도와주시든가.”
 58|
 59|곰곰이 생각하던 최 팀장이 대답했다.
 60|
 61|“그건 안 되겠네요. 제가 오늘 한정판을 입고 와서. 피라도 튀면 마음 아프잖습니까.”
 62|
 63|“……진짜 아프게 해 드려요?”
 64|
 65|대화를 이어 갈수록 내상을 입은 것처럼 속이 쓰리고 뒷골이 당긴다. 차라리 몬스터와 싸우는 게 낫지.
 66|
 67|성큼 앞으로 한 걸음 내딛는 내게 최 팀장이 한 마디를 툭 던졌다.
 68|
 69|“후퇴도 또 하나의 방법입니다.”
 70|
 71|한정판 장비에 피 튈까 봐 뒤에서 팔짱만 끼고 있는 인간이 제법 맞는 말을 한다. 처맞는 말.
 72|
 73|그리고…….
 74|
 75|“더 좋은 방법이 있는데 뭐 하러요?”
 76|
 77|저 앞. 리자드맨 대족장을 필두로 몬스터들이 파도처럼 밀려오고 있다. C급과 D급 몬스터가 뒤섞인, 평범한 C급 헌터라면 맞설 엄두도 못 낼 전력이었다.
 78|
 79|평범한 C급 헌터라면, 말이다.
 80|
 81|‘상태창 오픈.’
 82|
 83|띠링.
 84|
 85|시스템이 즉각 응답했다.
 86|
 87|헌터 일을 다시 시작하고 일주일이 지난 지금, 상태창에는 40레벨이라는 숫자와 맨 밑에 적힌 글씨가 반짝반짝 빛나고 있었다.
 88|
 89|
 90|
 91|- 잔여 포인트 : 100
 92|
 93|
 94|
 95|현실로 돌아온 이래 나는 한 번도 잔여 포인트를 쓰지 않았다. 순전히 호기심 때문이었다. 지금의 내가 어디까지 갈 수 있을까, 하는 의문.
 96|
 97|하지만 이 이상 아끼는 건 만용이다.
 98|
 99|‘근력, 체력에 각각 30. 민첩에 40 부여.’
100|
101|다음 순간, 잔여 포인트가 바닥을 드러냈다.
102|
103|하지만 그와는 반대로 내 몸속 깊숙한 곳에서는 새로운 힘이 솟구쳤다. 불과 몇 초전의 진태경과는 또 다른 내가 지금 이곳에 있었다.
104|
105|‘그래, 이거지.’
106|
107|희열감에 몸이 부르르 떨리던 그때.
108|
109|- 크아아아!
110|
111|리자드맨 대족장이 포효와 함께 돌진했다. 그림자를 드리운 거대한 철퇴를 향해, 나는 창을 뻗었다.
112|
113|“일섬(一晱).”
114|
115|창날의 끝에서, 바람의 길이 열렸다.
116|
117|
118|
119|* * *
120|
121|
122|
123|“허.”
124|
125|최 팀장, 최민우는 헛웃음을 흘렸다.
126|
127|늪지대를 감싸 안은 농밀한 피 안개, 그리고 그 아래 널브러진 몬스터들의 사체가 그의 눈에 비쳤다.
128|
129|‘이게 무슨.’
130|
131|보스 몬스터를 포함한 수십 마리의 몬스터가 한순간에 몰살당했다. 이 모든 게 고작 며칠 전 재각성한 C급 헌터의 창끝으로부터 벌어진 일이었다.
132|
133|‘이런 게 가능한가?’
134|
135|진태경을 처음 만난 날부터 품고 있던 의문이었다. 별생각 없이 E급 게이트에 갔던 그날, C급 헌터 두엇은 달라붙어야 하는 레어 몬스터를 압도적으로 밀어붙이던 그 모습.
136|
137|거기에 더해 지난 며칠 동안 그가 보여 준 힘은…….
138|
139|‘C급 헌터라니, 웃기지도 않지.’
140|
141|진태경과 단둘이 레이드를 시작한 이유는 간단했다.
142|
143|이 흥미로운 인물의 한계를 보기 위해서. 그리고 다른 이들에게 들키지 않기 위해서.
144|
145|그러나 문득 그런 생각이 들었다.
146|
147|‘혹시 나보다…….’
148|
149|아니, 아니다. 그럴 리가 없다.
150|
151|애써 이어지는 생각을 털어 내는 최민우의 눈에 진태경이 들어왔다. 그는 상반신이 날아간 보스 몬스터의 사체를 붙잡고 애통한 외침을 토해 내고 있었다.
152|
153|“안 돼! 내 가죽! 이거 비싼 건데!”
154|
155|……저런 인간이 그럴 리가 없지. 아니, 그러면 안 되지.
156|
157|최민우는 문득 억울해졌다.
158|
159|
160|
161|* * *
162|
163|
164|
165|불타는 금요일. 줄여서 불금.
166|
167|20대 청춘들은 무리지어 술 마시고, 클럽을 들락거리겠지만 나는 최 팀장과 게이트를 돌았다.
168|
169|오전에 한 번. 오후에 두 번. 그렇게 C급 게이트 세 번을 돌고 나오자 밖은 이미 어두운 밤이었다.
170|
171|“고생하셨습니다, 도련님.”
172|
173|이제는 익숙한 얼굴이다. 선 굵은 외모의 이 40대 아저씨를 최 팀장은 이렇게 불렀다.
174|
175|“김 집사님도 수고하셨어요.”
176|
177|김 집사. 비서도 아니고 집사다.
178|
179|워낙 현실성 없는 단어라 처음에는 잘못 들은 줄 알았다.
180|
181|‘나는 교회 집사밖에 못 만나 봤는데.’
182|
183|그는 일주일 용돈으로 천 원을 받던 나의 코흘리개 시절, 십일조로 백 원을 내라고 강요하던 불한당이었다.
184|
185|물론 나를 도련님이라고 불러 주지도 않았고, 심지어는 내가 십일조를 내기 싫다고 버티자 사탄의 자식이라고 중얼거렸다.
186|
187|그리고 일곱 살이었던 나는 궁금한 건 꼭 물어보는 성격이었다.
188|
189|
190|
191|‘엄마. 엄마가 사탄이야?’
192|
193|‘응? 사탄?’
194|
195|‘어. 교회 집사님이 그랬는데, 내가 사탄의 자식이래. 난 엄마 자식이니까 엄마가 사탄이지? 그치?’
196|
197|
198|
199|그 말이 엄마를 사탄으로 만들었다. 나는 두 번 다시 교회 떡볶이를 못 먹게 됐고 교회 집사는 주님 곁으로 갈 뻔했다.
200|
201|다시 생각해 보니 인생 진짜 버라이어티 하네.
202|
203|“하실 말씀이라도……?”
204|
205|김 집사의 말에 정신을 차렸다.
206|
207|“아무것도 아닙니다. 잠깐 다른 생각 좀 하느라.”
208|
209|“이제 퇴근합시다.”
210|
211|최 팀장은 어느새 사복 차림으로 갈아입었다. 얇은 맞춤 정장을 입은 모습이 꼭 연예인 같다.
212|
213|‘인생 진짜. 더럽게 불공평하네.’
214|
215|나는 내심 투덜거리며 장비를 벗기 시작했다. 물론 조심스러운 손길로. 첫날 검색해 봤는데 가격이…… 됐다, 말을 말자.
216|
217|김 집사가 장비를 건네받아 차에 싣는 사이, 나는 최 팀장에게 물었다.
218|
219|“내일은 몇 시에 나와야 합니까?”
220|
221|“내일 말입니까?”
222|
223|최 팀장이 의아한 듯한 목소리로 되묻는다.
224|
225|“오늘 금요일입니다.”
226|
227|“네.”
228|
229|“내일은 토요일이고요.”
230|
231|“금요일 다음이 토요일인 건 저도 알죠.”
232|
233|이게 누굴 병신으로 보나.
234|
235|“아니, 그러니까.”
236|
237|최 팀장이 눈썹을 찡그렸다.
238|
239|“설마, 주말도 일하시게요?”
240|
241|“……당연한 거 아니에요?”
242|
243|“…….”
244|
245|“…….”
246|
247|최 팀장이 충격받은 얼굴로 물었다.
248|
249|“아니, 주말에 안 쉬면 언제 쉽니까?”
250|
251|“음. 일 못 구할 때?”
252|
253|“그게 얼마나 되는데요.”
254|
255|“글쎄요. 많이 쉬면 한 달에 한 번?”
256|
257|“길드 소속이었잖습니까. 주말에도 출근했어요?”
258|
259|“했죠. 일 있으면.”
260|
261|“그거 헌터 근로법 위반 아닙니까?”
262|
263|완벽해 보이던 최 팀장도 모르는 게 딱 하나 있었다.
264|
265|세상 물정.
266|
267|나는 피식 웃었다.
268|
269|“그거 꼬박꼬박 지키는 중소 길드가 어디 있어요. 다들 추가 수당 더 얹어 주고 레이드 시키지. 뭐, 저야 좋지만.”
270|
271|“예? 좋다고요?”
272|
273|“주말에는 인력 사무소 가거든요. 그거 갈 바에야 길드에서 추가 수당 받는 게 훨씬 나으니까. 기록 남을까 봐 현찰로 딱딱 주고.”
274|
275|“…….”
276|
277|“뭐, 다 그런 거죠.”
278|
279|최 팀장이 고개를 절레절레 저었다.
280|
281|“우리 길드는 근로법 준수합니다. 가계약도 마찬가지예요.”
282|
283|그거 아쉽네. 이번 주말에는 인력 사무소에 가야 할 모양인가 보다.
284|
285|입맛을 다시는 나를 최 팀장이 특유의 묘한 눈빛으로 바라본다.
286|
287|“그렇게까지 하는 이유가 뭡니까?”
288|
289|“이유?”
290|
291|“이제 C급 헌터잖아요. 좀 쉬면서 해도 될 텐데요.”
292|
293|“그건…….”
294|
295|시스템이 언제 사라질지 몰라서요.
296|
297|목구멍에서 불쑥 튀어나오려는 말을 붙잡았다. 그건 누구한테도 말할 수 없는 나만의 비밀이다.
298|
299|“별 이유 없어요. 물 들어왔을 때 노 저어야죠.”
300|
301|“그렇게 일하다가는 노 부러집니다. 같이 배 타고 있는 사람도 생각하세요.”
302|
303|“같이 타고 있는 사람? 최 팀장님이요?”
304|
305|“뭐, 이를테면…….”
306|
307|최 팀장이 멈칫하더니 말을 이었다.
308|
309|“가족이라든가.”
310|
311|가족.
312|
313|고작 한 단어일 뿐인데, 몸 구석구석 온기가 스며든다. 통화는 가끔 하지만 벌써 두 달이 넘도록 보지 못했다. 무림에서의 시간까지 포함한다면 석 달이다.
314|
315|‘벌써 그렇게 됐나.’
316|
317|아버지가 돌아가신 이후 내 인생은 줄곧 오르막길을 달리는 차 같았다.
318|
319|그래서 엑셀만 밟을 수밖에 없었다. 발을 떼면 굴러떨어질 것 같아서. 금방이라도 시동이 꺼질 것 같아서.
320|
321|“아무튼 주말은 쉽니다. 인력 사무소 갈 생각하지 말고 쉬세요. 그거 계약 위반이니까.”
322|
323|“아, 네.”
324|
325|이렇게까지 억지로 쉬라는 거 보면 최 팀장 이 인간, 은근히 인성이 괜찮은…….
326|
327|아니지, 겨우 이 정도 감성 팔이에 넘어가면 안 되지. 그동안 나 혼자 어떤 개고생을 했는데.
328|
329|‘최 팀장은 악덕 고용주다. 악덕 고용주.’
330|
331|주말에 쉬라는 것도 당장 다음 주부터 대차게 부려 먹기 위함인 게 뻔했다. 엄한 데 체력 소모하지 말라는 노예 농장주의 마음가짐인 거지. 지독한 인간.
332|
333|“준비 끝났습니다, 도련님.”
334|
335|그때 장비를 실으러 갔던 김 집사가 돌아왔다.
336|
337|저 양반도 악덕 고용주 밑에서 고생이다. 밤 열 시가 다 돼 가도록 퇴근을 못 하고 있네.
338|
339|“아, 말씀드린 건요?”
340|
341|“가져왔습니다.”
342|
343|“드리세요.”
344|
345|악덕 고용주의 말에 김 집사가 손에 든 작은 박스를 내밀었다.
346|
347|“받으시죠, 헌터님.”
348|
349|나한테.
350|
351|“예? 저요?”
352|
353|보기에는 드링크병 박스 같은데. 눈만 끔뻑거리다가 머릿속을 번뜩 스치는 생각이 있어 조심스레 물었다.
354|

[P25]
The longer we talked, the more my gut burned and the back of my head throbbed, as if I were suffering an Internal Injury. I’d rather fight the monsters.

[P26]
As I strode forward, Team Leader Choi tossed out one last remark.

[P27]
“Retreat is another option.”

[P28]
The man standing behind me with his arms folded so blood wouldn’t splatter on his limited-edition Equipment had made a pretty good point.

[P29]
The kind that made me want to hit him.

[P30]
And yet…

[P31]
“Why bother when there’s a better way?”

[P32]
Ahead of us, the monsters surged forward like a wave, led by the Lizardman Great Chieftain. C- and D-rank monsters mixed together—a force an ordinary C-rank Hunter wouldn’t even dream of facing.

[P33]
An ordinary C-rank Hunter, that is.

[P34]
*Status Window, open.*

[P35]
Ding.

[P36]
The System answered at once.

[P37]
A week had passed since I’d started working as a Hunter again. On the Status Window, the number 40 and the line at the very bottom shone brightly.

[P38]
> **System**
>
> - Remaining Points: 100

[P39]
Since returning to reality, I hadn’t spent a single Remaining Point. Purely out of curiosity.

[P40]
*How far can I go as I am now?*

[P41]
But hoarding them any longer would be reckless.

[P42]
*Assign 30 each to Strength and Stamina. Assign 40 to Agility.*

[P43]
The next moment, my Remaining Points hit zero.

[P44]
In exchange, new power surged from deep inside me. I was no longer the same Jin Taekyung I’d been only seconds ago.

[P45]
*Yeah. This is it.*

[P46]
I was still trembling with exhilaration when—

[P47]
*Gwaaaar!*

[P48]
The Lizardman Great Chieftain charged with a roar. I thrust my spear toward the gigantic mace casting a shadow over me.

[P49]
“One Annihilation.”

[P50]
At the tip of my spear, a path through the wind opened.

[P51]
* * *

[P52]
“Hah.”

[P53]
Team Leader Choi—Choi Minwoo—let out a hollow laugh.

[P54]
A dense fog of blood hung over the wetlands, and beneath it lay the sprawled corpses of the monsters.

[P55]
*What the hell…*

[P56]
Dozens of monsters, including the boss, had been slaughtered in an instant. All of it by the spear of a C-rank Hunter who had reawakened only a few days ago.

[P57]
*Is something like this even possible?*

[P58]
It was a question he had carried since the day he first met Jin Taekyung.

[P59]
That day, they had entered an E-rank Gate without expecting much. There, Taekyung had completely overwhelmed a Rare Monster that normally would have taken two or three C-rank Hunters to bring down.

[P60]
And then there was the strength he had displayed over the past few days…

[P61]
*Calling him a C-rank Hunter is a joke.*

[P62]
The reason Choi had begun raiding alone with Taekyung was simple.

[P63]
He wanted to see how far this fascinating man could go.

[P64]
And he wanted to keep anyone else from finding out.

[P65]
But then a thought occurred to him.

[P66]
*Could he be stronger than me…?*

[P67]
No. Impossible.

[P68]
Choi Minwoo forced the thought aside. Then Jin Taekyung caught his eye.

[P69]
He was clutching the boss monster’s corpse—its upper body completely gone—and wailing in grief.

[P70]
“No! The hide! This stuff is expensive!”

[P71]
……There was no way a man like that could be.

[P72]
No. He *mustn’t* be.

[P73]
Choi Minwoo suddenly felt cheated.

[P74]
* * *

[P75]
Burning Friday. *Bulgeum*, for short.[^1]

[P76]
Other people in their twenties would be drinking in groups and drifting in and out of clubs. I spent it running Gates with Team Leader Choi.

[P77]
Once in the morning. Twice in the afternoon.

[P78]
By the time we finished three C-rank Gates and came back out, night had already fallen.

[P79]
“Thank you for your hard work, Young Master.”

[P80]
The face was familiar now. Team Leader Choi addressed the rugged-looking man in his forties like this:

[P81]
“Thank you for your hard work too, Butler Kim.”

[P82]
Butler Kim. Not a secretary—a *butler*.[^2]

[P83]
The word was so detached from reality that I thought I’d misheard it at first.

[P84]
*I’ve only ever met church deacons.*

[P85]
Back when I was a snot-nosed kid getting a thousand won a week in allowance, one of them had been the bastard who forced me to hand over a hundred won as a tithe.

[P86]
Of course, he hadn’t called me Young Master. When I dug in and refused to pay, he’d even muttered that I was the child of Satan.

[P87]
And at seven years old, I was the kind of kid who always asked when something made me curious.

[P88]
*Mom. Are you Satan?*

[P89]
*Huh? Satan?*

[P90]
*Yeah. The church deacon said I was Satan’s child. I’m your kid, so that makes you Satan, right? Right?*

[P91]
Those words turned my mother into Satan.

[P92]
I never got to eat the church tteokbokki again,[^3] and the church deacon nearly went to be with the Lord.

[P93]
Thinking back on it, my life really had been one hell of a variety show.

[P94]
“Did you have something to say…?”

[P95]
Butler Kim’s voice pulled me back.

[P96]
“Nothing. I was just thinking about something else.”

[P97]
“Let’s call it a day.”

[P98]
Team Leader Choi had already changed into street clothes. In a lightweight tailored suit, he looked just like a celebrity.

[P99]
*Life is so damn unfair.*

[P100]
I grumbled inwardly as I started taking off my Equipment. Carefully, of course. I’d looked up the price on the first day, and it was…

[P101]
Never mind. Let’s not go there.

[P102]
While Butler Kim loaded the Equipment into the car, I asked Team Leader Choi, “What time should I come in tomorrow?”

[P103]
“Tomorrow?”

[P104]
Team Leader Choi sounded puzzled.

[P105]
“Today is Friday.”

[P106]
“Yes.”

[P107]
“And tomorrow is Saturday.”

[P108]
“I know Saturday comes after Friday.”

[P109]
*Does he take me for a fucking idiot?*

[P110]
“No, I mean…”

[P111]
Team Leader Choi furrowed his brow.

[P112]
“Don’t tell me you’re planning to work this weekend too.”

[P113]
“……Isn’t that obvious?”

[P114]
“……”

[P115]
“……”

[P116]
Team Leader Choi stared at me in shock.

[P117]
“If you don’t take weekends off, when do you rest?”

[P118]
“Um. When I can’t find work?”

[P119]
“How often is that?”

[P120]
“I don’t know. If I get a lot of time off, maybe once a month?”

[P121]
“You used to belong to a Guild. You worked weekends then too?”

[P122]
“I did if there was work.”

[P123]
“Isn’t that a violation of the Hunter Labor Law?”

[P124]
Even Team Leader Choi, who seemed perfect, didn’t know one thing.

[P125]
How the world actually worked.

[P126]
I let out a short laugh.

[P127]
“What small or midsize Guild follows that to the letter? They all throw in extra pay and send you out on raids. Worked out for me, anyway.”

[P128]
“Excuse me? You *liked* it?”

[P129]
“I go to the day-labor agency on weekends. Getting extra pay from the Guild beats going there. They paid us cash on the spot to keep it off the books.”

[P130]
“……”

[P131]
“That’s just how it is.”

[P132]
Team Leader Choi shook his head in disbelief.

[P133]
“Our Guild follows the Labor Law. Provisional contracts are no exception.”

[P134]
*That’s a shame. Looks like I’ll have to go to the day-labor agency this weekend.*

[P135]
As I smacked my lips over the missed opportunity, Team Leader Choi gave me that peculiar look of his.

[P136]
“Why do you push yourself so hard?”

[P137]
“Why?”

[P138]
“You’re a C-rank Hunter now. You can afford to take it a little easier.”

[P139]
“That’s…”

[P140]
*Because I don’t know when the System might disappear.*

[P141]
I caught the words before they burst out of my throat. That was my secret—something I couldn’t tell anyone.

[P142]
“No particular reason. You have to row while the tide is in.”

[P143]
“If you keep working like that, you’ll break the oars. Think about the people in the boat with you.”

[P144]
“The people in the boat with me? You, Team Leader?”

[P145]
“Well, for example…”

[P146]
Team Leader Choi paused before continuing.

[P147]
“Your family.”

[P148]
Family.

[P149]
It was only one word, but warmth seeped into every corner of my body. We talked on the phone now and then, but I hadn’t seen them in more than two months. Counting the time I’d spent in Murim, it had been three.

[P150]
*Has it already been that long?*

[P151]
Ever since my father died, my life had felt like a car driving uphill.

[P152]
So I’d had no choice but to keep my foot on the gas. It felt as though I’d roll backward the moment I let up. As though the engine might die at any second.

[P153]
“Anyway, weekends are off. Don’t even think about going to the day-labor agency. Rest. That would be a contract violation.”

[P154]
“Oh. Okay.”

[P155]
*Forcing me to rest this hard… Maybe this guy Choi isn’t such a bad person after all…*

[P156]
No.

[P157]
I couldn’t let myself be taken in by a little sentimentality. Not after all the hell I’d gone through on my own.

[P158]
*Team Leader Choi is an exploitative employer. An exploitative employer.*

[P159]
It was obvious he only wanted me resting on the weekend so he could work me to the bone starting next week. It was the mentality of a slave plantation owner who didn’t want his worker wasting stamina somewhere else.

[P160]
What a vicious man.

[P161]
“Everything is ready, Young Master.”

[P162]
Butler Kim had returned after loading the Equipment.

[P163]
*That man’s suffering under an exploitative employer too. It’s almost ten at night, and he still hasn’t gotten off work.*

[P164]
“Ah. What about the thing I mentioned?”

[P165]
“I brought it.”

[P166]
“Give it to him.”

[P167]
At the exploitative employer’s command, Butler Kim held out the small box in his hands.

[P168]
“Please take this, Hunter.”

[P169]
He was offering it to me.

[P170]
“Huh? Me?”

[P171]
It looked like a box of tonic drinks. I blinked at it until a thought flashed through my mind.

[P172]
I asked carefully, “Don’t tell me this is money.”

[P173]
“We contracted for weekly pay. Did you forget?”

[P174]
I had. I’d assumed I would get it on Sunday.

[P175]
I took the box, still dazed. It was heavy.

[P176]
“Do you normally pay in cash?”

[P177]
“Of course not.”

[P178]
“Then…”

[P179]
“You said you preferred cash, Mr. Jin Taekyung. Especially crisp new bills.”

[P180]
I’d mentioned it in passing yesterday—or maybe the day before. I hadn’t expected anything to come of it.

[P181]
My opinion of the exploitative employer rose a little.

[P182]
*Of course, the most important part is still left.*

[P183]
Four days of pay, Tuesday through Friday. My first weekly paycheck as a C-rank Hunter.

[P184]
Of course I was excited to find out how much it was.

[P185]
I swallowed and opened my mouth.

[P186]
“Then how much is all of this…?”

[P187]
“I added a little extra on top of the contracted amount. The settlement details are inside, so check them. We’ll be going.”

[P188]
“Until next time, Hunter.”

[P189]
Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim took off in a flash.

[P190]
It all happened in an instant.

[P191]
I stared after the receding car lights, bewildered, then opened the drink box. In the faint moonlight, thick bundles of bills caught my eye.

[P192]
*One, two, three…*

[P193]
The count stopped at six.

[P194]
Six bundles of a hundred bills.

[P195]
In other words, six million won.

[P196]
“What is this?”

[P197]
*Scam.*

[P198]
The word flashed through my mind. Just as my legs were about to give out—

[P199]
“Huh?”

[P200]
Had I seen it wrong? Why were the bills yellowish?

[P201]
“Wait. Wait a second!”

[P202]
I focused internal energy into my eyes, and my vision brightened.

[P203]
Then I saw her.

[P204]
A kindly smiling woman in a hanbok, right there on the bill.

[P205]
“Shin Saimdang! Wise mother and virtuous wife! Her son is Yulgok Yi I! Her husband is Yi Wonsu!”

[P206]
I started speaking in tongues before I knew it.

[P207]
This was insane. Completely insane.

[P208]
One bundle held a hundred Shin Saimdang bills. Six of those meant…

[P209]
“Th-three hundred million!”

[P210]
This time I couldn’t catch myself as my legs gave out. I dropped to my knees with a thud and stared blankly into the drink box.

[P211]
Under the bundles, a white sheet of paper lined the bottom.

[P212]
*Right. The settlement sheet!*

[P213]
I unfolded it in a panic.

[P214]
It contained a complete record of the past four days’ earnings.

[P215]
Right down to the final amount being paid to me.

[P216]
*The settlement sheet says thirty million won.*

[P217]
What? Had I imagined it?

[P218]
I was confused. Completely confused.

[P219]
My shaking gaze froze on the final line.

[P220]
**Bonus: 270,000,000**

[P221]
Then I remembered Team Leader Choi’s last words before leaving.

[P222]
*I added a little extra on top of the contracted amount.*

[P223]
Thunder and lightning raged through my head.

[P224]
I rose on trembling legs. Far off in the distance, the car’s lights were already fading.

[P225]
They looked like a single ray of light.

[P226]
“Ahh. Aaaah…”

[P227]
Team Leader Choi.

[P228]
No—he was the Light.

[P229]
[^1]: Korean slang for Friday night, from “burning Friday.”
[^2]: In Korean, the same word, *jipsa*, means both butler and church deacon.
[^3]: Tteokbokki is a Korean dish of chewy rice cakes in a spicy sauce. Korean churches often sell it as a snack.

- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. ### Tone and Style

[P20]
“This is different. It’s a C-rank Gate.”

[P21]
“Then help, why don’t you.”

[P22]
Team Leader Choi thought it over before answering.

[P23]
“I don’t think I can. I’m wearing a limited edition today. It’d break my heart if blood splattered on it.”

[P24]
“……Should I make it hurt for real?”

[P25]
The longer we talked, the more my gut burned and the back of my head throbbed, as if I were suffering an Internal Injury. I’d rather fight the monsters.

[P26]
As I strode forward, Team Leader Choi tossed out one last remark.

[P27]
“Retreat is another option.”

[P28]
The man standing behind me with his arms folded so blood wouldn’t splatter on his limited-edition Equipment had made a pretty good point.

[P29]
The kind that made me want to hit him.

[P30]
And yet…

[P31]
“Why bother when there’s a better way?”

[P32]
Ahead of us, the monsters surged forward like a wave, led by the Lizardman Great Chieftain. C- and D-rank monsters mixed together—a force an ordinary C-rank Hunter wouldn’t even dream of facing.

[P33]
An ordinary C-rank Hunter, that is.

[P34]
*Status Window, open.*

[P35]
Ding.

[P36]
The System answered at once.

[P37]
A week had passed since I’d started working as a Hunter again. On the Status Window, the number 40 and the line at the very bottom shone brightly.

[P38]
> **System**
>
> - Remaining Points: 100

[P39]
Since returning to reality, I hadn’t spent a single Remaining Point. Purely out of curiosity.

[P40]
*How far can I go as I am now?*

[P41]
But hoarding them any longer would be reckless.

[P42]
*Assign 30 each to Strength and Stamina. Assign 40 to Agility.*

[P43]
The next moment, my Remaining Points hit zero.

[P44]
In exchange, new power surged from deep inside me. I was no longer the same Jin Taekyung I’d been only seconds ago.

[P45]
*Yeah. This is it.*

[P46]
I was still trembling with exhilaration when—

[P47]
*Gwaaaar!*

[P48]
The Lizardman Great Chieftain charged with a roar. I thrust my spear toward the gigantic mace casting a shadow over me.

[P49]
“One Annihilation.”

[P50]
At the tip of my spear, a path through the wind opened.

[P51]
* * *

[P52]
“Hah.”

[P53]
Team Leader Choi—Choi Minwoo—let out a hollow laugh.

[P54]
A dense fog of blood hung over the wetlands, and beneath it lay the sprawled corpses of the monsters.

[P55]
*What the hell…*

[P56]
Dozens of monsters, including the boss, had been slaughtered in an instant. All of it by the spear of a C-rank Hunter who had reawakened only a few days ago.

[P57]
*Is something like this even possible?*

[P58]
It was a question he had carried since the day he first met Jin Taekyung.

[P59]
That day, they had entered an E-rank Gate without expecting much. There, Taekyung had completely overwhelmed a Rare Monster that normally would have taken two or three C-rank Hunters to bring down.

[P60]
And then there was the strength he had displayed over the past few days…

[P61]
*Calling him a C-rank Hunter is a joke.*

[P62]
The reason Choi had begun raiding alone with Taekyung was simple.

[P63]
He wanted to see how far this fascinating man could go.

[P64]
And he wanted to keep anyone else from finding out.

[P65]
But then a thought occurred to him.

[P66]
*Could he be stronger than me…?*

[P67]
No. Impossible.

[P68]
Choi Minwoo forced the thought aside. Then Jin Taekyung caught his eye.

[P69]
He was clutching the boss monster’s corpse—its upper body completely gone—and wailing in grief.

[P70]
“No! The hide! This stuff is expensive!”

[P71]
……There was no way a man like that could be.

[P72]
No. He *mustn’t* be.

[P73]
Choi Minwoo suddenly felt cheated.

[P74]
* * *

[P75]
Burning Friday. *Bulgeum*, for short.[^1]

[P76]
Other people in their twenties would be drinking in groups and drifting in and out of clubs. I spent it running Gates with Team Leader Choi.

[P77]
Once in the morning. Twice in the afternoon.

[P78]
By the time we finished three C-rank Gates and came back out, night had already fallen.

[P79]
“Thank you for your hard work, Young Master.”

[P80]
The face was familiar now. Team Leader Choi addressed the rugged-looking man in his forties like this:

[P81]
“Thank you for your hard work too, Butler Kim.”

[P82]
Butler Kim. Not a secretary—a *butler*.[^2]

[P83]
The word was so detached from reality that I thought I’d misheard it at first.

[P84]
*I’ve only ever met church deacons.*

[P85]
Back when I was a snot-nosed kid getting a thousand won a week in allowance, one of them had been the bastard who forced me to hand over a hundred won as a tithe.

[P86]
Of course, he hadn’t called me Young Master. When I dug in and refused to pay, he’d even muttered that I was the child of Satan.

[P87]
And at seven years old, I was the kind of kid who always asked when something made me curious.

[P88]
*Mom. Are you Satan?*

[P89]
*Huh? Satan?*

[P90]
*Yeah. The church deacon said I was Satan’s child. I’m your kid, so that makes you Satan, right? Right?*

[P91]
Those words turned my mother into Satan.

[P92]
I never got to eat the church tteokbokki again,[^3] and the church deacon nearly went to be with the Lord.

[P93]
Thinking back on it, my life really had been one hell of a variety show.

[P94]
“Did you have something to say…?”

[P95]
Butler Kim’s voice pulled me back.

[P96]
“Nothing. I was just thinking about something else.”

[P97]
“Let’s call it a day.”

[P98]
Team Leader Choi had already changed into street clothes. In a lightweight tailored suit, he looked just like a celebrity.

[P99]
*Life is so damn unfair.*

[P100]
I grumbled inwardly as I started taking off my Equipment. Carefully, of course. I’d looked up the price on the first day, and it was…

[P101]
Never mind. Let’s not go there.

[P102]
While Butler Kim loaded the Equipment into the car, I asked Team Leader Choi, “What time should I come in tomorrow?”

[P103]
“Tomorrow?”

[P104]
Team Leader Choi sounded puzzled.

[P105]
“Today is Friday.”

[P106]
“Yes.”

[P107]
“And tomorrow is Saturday.”

[P108]
“I know Saturday comes after Friday.”

[P109]
*Does he take me for a fucking idiot?*

[P110]
“No, I mean…”

[P111]
Team Leader Choi furrowed his brow.

[P112]
“Don’t tell me you’re planning to work this weekend too.”

[P113]
“……Isn’t that obvious?”

[P114]
“……”

[P115]
“……”

[P116]
Team Leader Choi stared at me in shock.

[P117]
“If you don’t take weekends off, when do you rest?”

[P118]
“Um. When I can’t find work?”

[P119]
“How often is that?”

[P120]
“I don’t know. If I get a lot of time off, maybe once a month?”

[P121]
“You used to belong to a Guild. You worked weekends then too?”

[P122]
“I did if there was work.”

[P123]
“Isn’t that a violation of the Hunter Labor Law?”

[P124]
Even Team Leader Choi, who seemed perfect, didn’t know one thing.

[P125]
How the world actually worked.

[P126]
I let out a short laugh.

[P127]
“What small or midsize Guild follows that to the letter? They all throw in extra pay and send you out on raids. Worked out for me, anyway.”

[P128]
“Excuse me? You *liked* it?”

[P129]
“I go to the day-labor agency on weekends. Getting extra pay from the Guild beats going there. They paid us cash on the spot to keep it off the books.”

[P130]
“……”

[P131]
“That’s just how it is.”

[P132]
Team Leader Choi shook his head in disbelief.

[P133]
“Our Guild follows the Labor Law. Provisional contracts are no exception.”

[P134]
*That’s a shame. Looks like I’ll have to go to the day-labor agency this weekend.*

[P135]
As I smacked my lips over the missed opportunity, Team Leader Choi gave me that peculiar look of his.

[P136]
“Why do you push yourself so hard?”

[P137]
“Why?”

[P138]
“You’re a C-rank Hunter now. You can afford to take it a little easier.”

[P139]
“That’s…”

[P140]
*Because I don’t know when the System might disappear.*

[P141]
I caught the words before they burst out of my throat. That was my secret—something I couldn’t tell anyone.

[P142]
“No particular reason. You have to row while the tide is in.”

[P143]
“If you keep working like that, you’ll break the oars. Think about the people in the boat with you.”

[P144]
“The people in the boat with me? You, Team Leader?”

[P145]
“Well, for example…”

[P146]
Team Leader Choi paused before continuing.

[P147]
“Your family.”

[P148]
Family.

[P149]
It was only one word, but warmth seeped into every corner of my body. We talked on the phone now and then, but I hadn’t seen them in more than two months. Counting the time I’d spent in Murim, it had been three.

[P150]
*Has it already been that long?*

[P151]
Ever since my father died, my life had felt like a car driving uphill.

[P152]
So I’d had no choice but to keep my foot on the gas. It felt as though I’d roll backward the moment I let up. As though the engine might die at any second.

[P153]
“Anyway, weekends are off. Don’t even think about going to the day-labor agency. Rest. That would be a contract violation.”

[P154]
“Oh. Okay.”

[P155]
*Forcing me to rest this hard… Maybe this guy Choi isn’t such a bad person after all…*

[P156]
No.

[P157]
I couldn’t let myself be taken in by a little sentimentality. Not after all the hell I’d gone through on my own.

[P158]
*Team Leader Choi is an exploitative employer. An exploitative employer.*

[P159]
It was obvious he only wanted me resting on the weekend so he could work me to the bone starting next week. It was the mentality of a slave plantation owner who didn’t want his worker wasting stamina somewhere else.

[P160]
What a vicious man.

[P161]
“Everything is ready, Young Master.”

[P162]
Butler Kim had returned after loading the Equipment.

[P163]
*That man’s suffering under an exploitative employer too. It’s almost ten at night, and he still hasn’t gotten off work.*

[P164]
“Ah. What about the thing I mentioned?”

[P165]
“I brought it.”

[P166]
“Give it to him.”

[P167]
At the exploitative employer’s command, Butler Kim held out the small box in his hands.

[P168]
“Please take this, Hunter.”

[P169]
He was offering it to me.

[P170]
“Huh? Me?”

[P171]
It looked like a box of tonic drinks. I blinked at it until a thought flashed through my mind.

[P172]
I asked carefully, “Don’t tell me this is money.”

[P173]
“We contracted for weekly pay. Did you forget?”

[P174]
I had. I’d assumed I would get it on Sunday.

[P175]
I took the box, still dazed. It was heavy.

[P176]
“Do you normally pay in cash?”

[P177]
“Of course not.”

[P178]
“Then…”

[P179]
“You said you preferred cash, Mr. Jin Taekyung. Especially crisp new bills.”

[P180]
I’d mentioned it in passing yesterday—or maybe the day before. I hadn’t expected anything to come of it.

[P181]
My opinion of the exploitative employer rose a little.

[P182]
*Of course, the most important part is still left.*

[P183]
Four days of pay, Tuesday through Friday. My first weekly paycheck as a C-rank Hunter.

[P184]
Of course I was excited to find out how much it was.

[P185]
I swallowed and opened my mouth.

[P186]
“Then how much is all of this…?”

[P187]
“I added a little extra on top of the contracted amount. The settlement details are inside, so check them. We’ll be going.”

[P188]
“Until next time, Hunter.”

[P189]
Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim took off in a flash.

[P190]
It all happened in an instant.

[P191]
I stared after the receding car lights, bewildered, then opened the drink box. In the faint moonlight, thick bundles of bills caught my eye.

[P192]
*One, two, three…*

[P193]
The count stopped at six.

[P194]
Six bundles of a hundred bills.

[P195]
In other words, six million won.

[P196]
“What is this?”

[P197]
*Scam.*

[P198]
The word flashed through my mind. Just as my legs were about to give out—

[P199]
“Huh?”

[P200]
Had I seen it wrong? Why were the bills yellowish?

[P201]
“Wait. Wait a second!”

[P202]
I focused internal energy into my eyes, and my vision brightened.

[P203]
Then I saw her.

[P204]
A kindly smiling woman in a hanbok, right there on the bill.

[P205]
“Shin Saimdang! Wise mother and virtuous wife! Her son is Yulgok Yi I! Her husband is Yi Wonsu!”

[P206]
I started speaking in tongues before I knew it.

[P207]
This was insane. Completely insane.

[P208]
One bundle held a hundred Shin Saimdang bills. Six of those meant…

[P209]
“Th-three hundred million!”

[P210]
This time I couldn’t catch myself as my legs gave out. I dropped to my knees with a thud and stared blankly into the drink box.

[P211]
Under the bundles, a white sheet of paper lined the bottom.

[P212]
*Right. The settlement sheet!*

[P213]
I unfolded it in a panic.

[P214]
It contained a complete record of the past four days’ earnings.

[P215]
Right down to the final amount being paid to me.

[P216]
*The settlement sheet says thirty million won.*

[P217]
What? Had I imagined it?

[P218]
I was confused. Completely confused.

[P219]
My shaking gaze froze on the final line.

[P220]
**Bonus: 270,000,000**

[P221]
Then I remembered Team Leader Choi’s last words before leaving.

[P222]
*I added a little extra on top of the contracted amount.*

[P223]
Thunder and lightning raged through my head.

[P224]
I rose on trembling legs. Far off in the distance, the car’s lights were already fading.

[P225]
They looked like a single ray of light.

[P226]
“Ahh. Aaaah…”

[P227]
Team Leader Choi.

[P228]
No—he was the Light.

[P229]
[^1]: Korean slang for Friday night, from “burning Friday.”
[^2]: In Korean, the same word, *jipsa*, means both butler and church deacon.
[^3]: Tteokbokki is a Korean dish of chewy rice cakes in a spicy sauce. Korean churches often sell it as a snack.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Team Leader Choi—Choi Minwoo—let out a hollow laugh.

[P54]
A dense fog of blood hung over the wetlands, and beneath it lay the sprawled corpses of the monsters.

[P55]
*What the hell…*

[P56]
Dozens of monsters, including the boss, had been slaughtered in an instant. All of it by the spear of a C-rank Hunter who had reawakened only a few days ago.

[P57]
*Is something like this even possible?*

[P58]
It was a question he had carried since the day he first met Jin Taekyung.

[P59]
That day, they had entered an E-rank Gate without expecting much. There, Taekyung had completely overwhelmed a Rare Monster that normally would have taken two or three C-rank Hunters to bring down.

[P60]
And then there was the strength he had displayed over the past few days…

[P61]
*Calling him a C-rank Hunter is a joke.*

[P62]
The reason Choi had begun raiding alone with Taekyung was simple.

[P63]
He wanted to see how far this fascinating man could go.

[P64]
And he wanted to keep anyone else from finding out.

[P65]
But then a thought occurred to him.

[P66]
*Could he be stronger than me…?*

[P67]
No. Impossible.

[P68]
Choi Minwoo forced the thought aside. Then Jin Taekyung caught his eye.

[P69]
He was clutching the boss monster’s corpse—its upper body completely gone—and wailing in grief.

[P70]
“No! The hide! This stuff is expensive!”

[P71]
……There was no way a man like that could be.

[P72]
No. He *mustn’t* be.

[P73]
Choi Minwoo suddenly felt cheated.

[P74]
* * *

[P75]
Burning Friday. *Bulgeum*, for short.[^1]

[P76]
Other people in their twenties would be drinking in groups and drifting in and out of clubs. I spent it running Gates with Team Leader Choi.

[P77]
Once in the morning. Twice in the afternoon.

[P78]
By the time we finished three C-rank Gates and came back out, night had already fallen.

[P79]
“Thank you for your hard work, Young Master.”

[P80]
The face was familiar now. Team Leader Choi addressed the rugged-looking man in his forties like this:

[P81]
“Thank you for your hard work too, Butler Kim.”

[P82]
Butler Kim. Not a secretary—a *butler*.[^2]

[P83]
The word was so detached from reality that I thought I’d misheard it at first.

[P84]
*I’ve only ever met church deacons.*

[P85]
Back when I was a snot-nosed kid getting a thousand won a week in allowance, one of them had been the bastard who forced me to hand over a hundred won as a tithe.

[P86]
Of course, he hadn’t called me Young Master. When I dug in and refused to pay, he’d even muttered that I was the child of Satan.

[P87]
And at seven years old, I was the kind of kid who always asked when something made me curious.

[P88]
*Mom. Are you Satan?*

[P89]
*Huh? Satan?*

[P90]
*Yeah. The church deacon said I was Satan’s child. I’m your kid, so that makes you Satan, right? Right?*

[P91]
Those words turned my mother into Satan.

[P92]
I never got to eat the church tteokbokki again,[^3] and the church deacon nearly went to be with the Lord.

[P93]
Thinking back on it, my life really had been one hell of a variety show.

[P94]
“Did you have something to say…?”

[P95]
Butler Kim’s voice pulled me back.

[P96]
“Nothing. I was just thinking about something else.”

[P97]
“Let’s call it a day.”

[P98]
Team Leader Choi had already changed into street clothes. In a lightweight tailored suit, he looked just like a celebrity.

[P99]
*Life is so damn unfair.*

[P100]
I grumbled inwardly as I started taking off my Equipment. Carefully, of course. I’d looked up the price on the first day, and it was…

[P101]
Never mind. Let’s not go there.

[P102]
While Butler Kim loaded the Equipment into the car, I asked Team Leader Choi, “What time should I come in tomorrow?”

[P103]
“Tomorrow?”

[P104]
Team Leader Choi sounded puzzled.

[P105]
“Today is Friday.”

[P106]
“Yes.”

[P107]
“And tomorrow is Saturday.”

[P108]
“I know Saturday comes after Friday.”

[P109]
*Does he take me for a fucking idiot?*

[P110]
“No, I mean…”

[P111]
Team Leader Choi furrowed his brow.

[P112]
“Don’t tell me you’re planning to work this weekend too.”

[P113]
“……Isn’t that obvious?”

[P114]
“……”

[P115]
“……”

[P116]
Team Leader Choi stared at me in shock.

[P117]
“If you don’t take weekends off, when do you rest?”

[P118]
“Um. When I can’t find work?”

[P119]
“How often is that?”

[P120]
“I don’t know. If I get a lot of time off, maybe once a month?”

[P121]
“You used to belong to a Guild. You worked weekends then too?”

[P122]
“I did if there was work.”

[P123]
“Isn’t that a violation of the Hunter Labor Law?”

[P124]
Even Team Leader Choi, who seemed perfect, didn’t know one thing.

[P125]
How the world actually worked.

[P126]
I let out a short laugh.

[P127]
“What small or midsize Guild follows that to the letter? They all throw in extra pay and send you out on raids. Worked out for me, anyway.”

[P128]
“Excuse me? You *liked* it?”

[P129]
“I go to the day-labor agency on weekends. Getting extra pay from the Guild beats going there. They paid us cash on the spot to keep it off the books.”

[P130]
“……”

[P131]
“That’s just how it is.”

[P132]
Team Leader Choi shook his head in disbelief.

[P133]
“Our Guild follows the Labor Law. Provisional contracts are no exception.”

[P134]
*That’s a shame. Looks like I’ll have to go to the day-labor agency this weekend.*

[P135]
As I smacked my lips over the missed opportunity, Team Leader Choi gave me that peculiar look of his.

[P136]
“Why do you push yourself so hard?”

[P137]
“Why?”

[P138]
“You’re a C-rank Hunter now. You can afford to take it a little easier.”

[P139]
“That’s…”

[P140]
*Because I don’t know when the System might disappear.*

[P141]
I caught the words before they burst out of my throat. That was my secret—something I couldn’t tell anyone.

[P142]
“No particular reason. You have to row while the tide is in.”

[P143]
“If you keep working like that, you’ll break the oars. Think about the people in the boat with you.”

[P144]
“The people in the boat with me? You, Team Leader?”

[P145]
“Well, for example…”

[P146]
Team Leader Choi paused before continuing.

[P147]
“Your family.”

[P148]
Family.

[P149]
It was only one word, but warmth seeped into every corner of my body. We talked on the phone now and then, but I hadn’t seen them in more than two months. Counting the time I’d spent in Murim, it had been three.

[P150]
*Has it already been that long?*

[P151]
Ever since my father died, my life had felt like a car driving uphill.

[P152]
So I’d had no choice but to keep my foot on the gas. It felt as though I’d roll backward the moment I let up. As though the engine might die at any second.

[P153]
“Anyway, weekends are off. Don’t even think about going to the day-labor agency. Rest. That would be a contract violation.”

[P154]
“Oh. Okay.”

[P155]
*Forcing me to rest this hard… Maybe this guy Choi isn’t such a bad person after all…*

[P156]
No.

[P157]
I couldn’t let myself be taken in by a little sentimentality. Not after all the hell I’d gone through on my own.

[P158]
*Team Leader Choi is an exploitative employer. An exploitative employer.*

[P159]
It was obvious he only wanted me resting on the weekend so he could work me to the bone starting next week. It was the mentality of a slave plantation owner who didn’t want his worker wasting stamina somewhere else.

[P160]
What a vicious man.

[P161]
“Everything is ready, Young Master.”

[P162]
Butler Kim had returned after loading the Equipment.

[P163]
*That man’s suffering under an exploitative employer too. It’s almost ten at night, and he still hasn’t gotten off work.*

[P164]
“Ah. What about the thing I mentioned?”

[P165]
“I brought it.”

[P166]
“Give it to him.”

[P167]
At the exploitative employer’s command, Butler Kim held out the small box in his hands.

[P168]
“Please take this, Hunter.”

[P169]
He was offering it to me.

[P170]
“Huh? Me?”

[P171]
It looked like a box of tonic drinks. I blinked at it until a thought flashed through my mind.

[P172]
I asked carefully, “Don’t tell me this is money.”

[P173]
“We contracted for weekly pay. Did you forget?”

[P174]
I had. I’d assumed I would get it on Sunday.

[P175]
I took the box, still dazed. It was heavy.

[P176]
“Do you normally pay in cash?”

[P177]
“Of course not.”

[P178]
“Then…”

[P179]
“You said you preferred cash, Mr. Jin Taekyung. Especially crisp new bills.”

[P180]
I’d mentioned it in passing yesterday—or maybe the day before. I hadn’t expected anything to come of it.

[P181]
My opinion of the exploitative employer rose a little.

[P182]
*Of course, the most important part is still left.*

[P183]
Four days of pay, Tuesday through Friday. My first weekly paycheck as a C-rank Hunter.

[P184]
Of course I was excited to find out how much it was.

[P185]
I swallowed and opened my mouth.

[P186]
“Then how much is all of this…?”

[P187]
“I added a little extra on top of the contracted amount. The settlement details are inside, so check them. We’ll be going.”

[P188]
“Until next time, Hunter.”

[P189]
Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim took off in a flash.

[P190]
It all happened in an instant.

[P191]
I stared after the receding car lights, bewildered, then opened the drink box. In the faint moonlight, thick bundles of bills caught my eye.

[P192]
*One, two, three…*

[P193]
The count stopped at six.

[P194]
Six bundles of a hundred bills.

[P195]
In other words, six million won.

[P196]
“What is this?”

[P197]
*Scam.*

[P198]
The word flashed through my mind. Just as my legs were about to give out—

[P199]
“Huh?”

[P200]
Had I seen it wrong? Why were the bills yellowish?

[P201]
“Wait. Wait a second!”

[P202]
I focused internal energy into my eyes, and my vision brightened.

[P203]
Then I saw her.

[P204]
A kindly smiling woman in a hanbok, right there on the bill.

[P205]
“Shin Saimdang! Wise mother and virtuous wife! Her son is Yulgok Yi I! Her husband is Yi Wonsu!”

[P206]
I started speaking in tongues before I knew it.

[P207]
This was insane. Completely insane.

[P208]
One bundle held a hundred Shin Saimdang bills. Six of those meant…

[P209]
“Th-three hundred million!”

[P210]
This time I couldn’t catch myself as my legs gave out. I dropped to my knees with a thud and stared blankly into the drink box.

[P211]
Under the bundles, a white sheet of paper lined the bottom.

[P212]
*Right. The settlement sheet!*

[P213]
I unfolded it in a panic.

[P214]
It contained a complete record of the past four days’ earnings.

[P215]
Right down to the final amount being paid to me.

[P216]
*The settlement sheet says thirty million won.*

[P217]
What? Had I imagined it?

[P218]
I was confused. Completely confused.

[P219]
My shaking gaze froze on the final line.

[P220]
**Bonus: 270,000,000**

[P221]
Then I remembered Team Leader Choi’s last words before leaving.

[P222]
*I added a little extra on top of the contracted amount.*

[P223]
Thunder and lightning raged through my head.

[P224]
I rose on trembling legs. Far off in the distance, the car’s lights were already fading.

[P225]
They looked like a single ray of light.

[P226]
“Ahh. Aaaah…”

[P227]
Team Leader Choi.

[P228]
No—he was the Light.

[P229]
[^1]: Korean slang for Friday night, from “burning Friday.”
[^2]: In Korean, the same word, *jipsa*, means both butler and church deacon.
[^3]: Tteokbokki is a Korean dish of chewy rice cakes in a spicy sauce. Korean churches often sell it as a snack.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.
